title: Yellow Japanese Azuki Beans Zenzai
description: A traditional Japanese dessert originating from Kyushu, made with azuki beans and featuring a unique winey flavor, this diabetic-friendly version incorporates branston pickle and sous-vide cooking for a modern twist.
instructions: Rinse the azuki beans and soak them in water for at least 4 hours.
Drain and rinse the soaked azuki beans, then place them in a sous-vide bag with 2 cups of water and cook at 180 degrees Fahrenheit for 4 hours.
In a blender or food processor, puree the cooked azuki beans with the remaining 2 cups of water until smooth.
In a saucepan, combine the pureed azuki beans, sugar substitute, and salt, and heat over low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture is warm and well combined.
Stir in the chopped branston pickle and sake, if using.
Pour the mixture into individual serving cups and chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Just before serving, use a whisk or electric mixer to aerate the zenzai until it becomes light and fluffy.
Serve the Yellow Japanese Azuki Beans Zenzai chilled, garnished with additional branston pickle if desired.
Refrigerate and consume within 1 week — this preparation is not shelf-stable without an approved acid level and canning process.

Refrigerator pickle only: store in the fridge and consume within 1 week. For shelf-stable canning, add at least 2 tablespoons of vinegar (5% acidity) per cup of brine and follow a tested water-bath process.
